inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made it harder to revoke pre-arrest bail, requiring clear proof that someone misused their liberty or that circumstances changed—even when stolen articles remain missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the plea to cancel bail in a house case. It is presented as a safeguard, but its effect is a ready-made shield: the public must prove what may be kept out of sight, while the accused remains protected under rules that are said to have been followed.
